---
name: CI

# yamllint disable-line rule:truthy
on:
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - "*"
  push:
    branches:
      - master

concurrency:
  group: build-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  unit-tests:
    name: unit-tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    strategy:
      # both versions are reported, because knowing a change works on one and
      # not the other is the point of running it against two
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        dokku_version:
          # the version being developed against
          - master
          # the oldest dokku that runs on this runner: 0.35.0 is where ubuntu
          # 24.04 became a supported distribution, and 0.34.9 before it tops
          # out at 22.04
          - "0.35.0"
    env:
      DOKKU_VERSION: ${{ matrix.dokku_version }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"

      - run: make setup

      - run: sudo sysctl -w vm.max_map_count=262144

      - if: matrix.dokku_version == 'master'
        run: |
          make generate
          if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain -- README.md datastore)" ]; then
            echo "Please run 'make generate'"
            git status --short
            git --no-pager diff
            exit 1
          fi

      - run: make test

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        if: failure()
        with:
          name: test-results-${{ matrix.dokku_version }}
          path: test-results

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -eo pipefail
[[ $TRACE ]] && set -x
sudo apt-key adv --keyserver keyserver.ubuntu.com --recv-keys 762E3157
echo "deb http://nginx.org/packages/ubuntu $(lsb_release -cs) nginx" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/nginx.list
curl -fsSL https://nginx.org/keys/nginx_signing.key | sudo apt-key add -

sudo mkdir -p /etc/nginx
sudo curl https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dokku/dokku/master/tests/dhparam.pem -o /etc/nginx/dhparam.pem

echo "dokku dokku/skip_key_file boolean true" | sudo debconf-set-selections
wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dokku/dokku/master/bootstrap.sh
if [[ "$DOKKU_VERSION" == "master" ]]; then
  sudo bash bootstrap.sh
else
  sudo DOKKU_TAG="$DOKKU_VERSION" bash bootstrap.sh
fi
echo "Dokku version $DOKKU_VERSION"

export DOKKU_LIB_ROOT="/var/lib/dokku"
export DOKKU_PLUGINS_ROOT="$DOKKU_LIB_ROOT/plugins/available"
pushd "$(dirname "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)")" >/dev/null
source "config"
popd >/dev/null
sudo rm -rf "$DOKKU_PLUGINS_ROOT/$PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX"
sudo mkdir -p "$DOKKU_PLUGINS_ROOT/$PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX" "$DOKKU_PLUGINS_ROOT/$PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX/subcommands" "$DOKKU_PLUGINS_ROOT/$PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX/scripts" "$DOKKU_PLUGINS_ROOT/$PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX/templates"
sudo find ./ -maxdepth 1 -type f -exec cp '{}' "$DOKKU_PLUGINS_ROOT/$PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX" \;
[[ -d "./scripts" ]] && sudo find ./scripts -maxdepth 1 -type f -exec cp '{}' "$DOKKU_PLUGINS_ROOT/$PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX/scripts" \;
[[ -d "./subcommands" ]] && sudo find ./subcommands -maxdepth 1 -type f -exec cp '{}' "$DOKKU_PLUGINS_ROOT/$PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX/subcommands" \;
[[ -d "./templates" ]] && sudo find ./templates -maxdepth 1 -type f -exec cp '{}' "$DOKKU_PLUGINS_ROOT/$PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX/templates" \;
# recursive rather than the flat copies above, because a definition is a tree: it
# has a rootfs and a bin below it. Without this the plugin's own definitions are
# missing under test and the embedded ones answer instead, so an override would
# work in production and quietly vanish here.
[[ -d "./datastore" ]] && sudo cp -R ./datastore "$DOKKU_PLUGINS_ROOT/$PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX/"
sudo mkdir -p "$PLUGIN_CONFIG_ROOT" "$PLUGIN_DATA_ROOT"
sudo dokku plugin:enable "$PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX"

# stage a locally built dokku-datastore so that an unreleased build can be
# tested against this plugin, rather than the version pinned in config
if [[ -n "$DOKKU_DATASTORE_BINARY" ]]; then
  echo "Staging dokku-datastore from $DOKKU_DATASTORE_BINARY"
  sudo mkdir -p "$DOKKU_LIB_ROOT/data/$PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX"
  sudo cp "$DOKKU_DATASTORE_BINARY" "$DOKKU_LIB_ROOT/data/$PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX/dokku-datastore.local"
  sudo chmod +x "$DOKKU_LIB_ROOT/data/$PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX/dokku-datastore.local"
fi

sudo dokku plugin:install

# Extra Documentation

The documentation in this folder is supplemental to using this plugin. It is injected automatically into the plugin's readme during documentation generation.

#!/usr/bin/env bats
load test_helper

setup() {
  dokku apps:create my-app
  dokku "$PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX:create" ls
  dokku "$PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX:link" ls my-app >&2
}

teardown() {
  dokku "$PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX:unlink" ls renamed-app >&2 || true
  clear_links ls
  dokku "$PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX:destroy" ls -f || true
  dokku apps:destroy my-app --force || true
  dokku apps:destroy renamed-app --force || true
}

# this trigger only adds the new name. The old one goes when the rename destroys
# the app it belonged to, since that fires the pre-delete this plugin installs,
# so it takes both halves for the service to end up linked to the app that is
# actually there. --skip-deploy keeps a never deployed app from rebuilding.
@test "($PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX:hook:post-app-rename-setup) moves the link onto the new name" {
  dokku apps:rename --skip-deploy my-app renamed-app

  run sudo cat "$PLUGIN_DATA_ROOT/ls/LINKS"
  echo "output: $output"
  echo "status: $status"
  assert_contains "${lines[*]}" "renamed-app"
  assert_not_contains "${lines[*]}" "my-app"

  run dokku "$PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX:links" ls
  echo "output: $output"
  echo "status: $status"
  assert_success
  assert_contains "${lines[*]}" "renamed-app"
  assert_not_contains "${lines[*]}" "my-app"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
source "$(dirname "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)")/config"
set -eo pipefail
[[ $DOKKU_TRACE ]] && set -x

service-backup-auth-cmd() {
  declare desc="set up authentication for backups on the $PLUGIN_SERVICE service"
  local cmd="$PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX:backup-auth" argv=("$@")
  [[ ${argv[0]} == "$cmd" ]] && shift 1

  "${DOKKU_LIB_ROOT}/data/${PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX}/dokku-datastore" backup-auth "$PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX" "$@"
}

service-backup-auth-cmd "$@"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
source "$(dirname "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)")/config"
set -eo pipefail
[[ $DOKKU_TRACE ]] && set -x

service-backup-deauth-cmd() {
  declare desc="remove backup authentication for the $PLUGIN_SERVICE service"
  local cmd="$PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX:backup-deauth" argv=("$@")
  [[ ${argv[0]} == "$cmd" ]] && shift 1

  "${DOKKU_LIB_ROOT}/data/${PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX}/dokku-datastore" backup-deauth "$PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX" "$@"
}

service-backup-deauth-cmd "$@"

---
name: "tagged-release"

# yamllint disable-line rule:truthy
on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "*"

jobs:
  tagged-release:
    name: tagged-release
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04

    steps:
      - name: Release
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v3
        with:
          generate_release_notes: true
          make_latest: "true"

---
name: "upgrade-dokku-datastore"

# yamllint disable-line rule:truthy
on:
  schedule:
    # daily, off the hour so it is not queued behind everything that runs at one
    - cron: "17 6 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  upgrade:
    name: upgrade
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    env:
      # a pull request opened with the default GITHUB_TOKEN does not start any
      # workflow, which would leave the bump with no tests at all. A personal
      # token is used when the repository has one so that CI runs on what it
      # opens; without one the pull request still appears, and needs a push or a
      # reopen to be checked.
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_ACCESS_TOKEN || github.token }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.GH_ACCESS_TOKEN || github.token }}

      - name: Compare the pinned version with the released one
        id: versions
        run: |
          current="$(make -s datastore-version)"
          latest="$(gh release view --repo dokku/dokku-datastore --json tagName --jq .tagName)"
          echo "pinned $current, released $latest"

          {
            echo "current=$current"
            echo "latest=$latest"
            echo "branch=dokku-datastore-$latest"
          } >>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

          # forward only: an unexpected answer must not roll the plugin back to
          # a release older than the one it already pins
          newest="$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$current" "$latest" | sort -V | tail -1)"
          if [[ "$current" == "$latest" ]] || [[ "$newest" != "$latest" ]]; then
            echo "upgrade=false" >>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "upgrade=true" >>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      # any state, so that a bump somebody closed on purpose is not reopened
      # every morning
      - name: Check whether this bump has been proposed already
        id: proposed
        if: steps.versions.outputs.upgrade == 'true'
        run: |
          existing="$(gh pr list --head "$BRANCH" --state all --json number --jq '.[0].number')"
          if [[ -n "$existing" ]]; then
            echo "already proposed as #$existing"
            echo "open=true" >>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "open=false" >>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
        env:
          BRANCH: ${{ steps.versions.outputs.branch }}

      - name: Bump the pin and regenerate what it produces
        id: bump
        if: steps.versions.outputs.upgrade == 'true' && steps.proposed.outputs.open == 'false'
        run: |
          # the whole line is rewritten rather than the version substituted, so
          # that nothing depends on escaping the dots in the version being right
          line='export DOKKU_DATASTORE_VERSION="${DOKKU_DATASTORE_VERSION:-'"$LATEST"'}"'
          sed -i "s|^export DOKKU_DATASTORE_VERSION=.*|$line|" config

          # a sed that matched nothing would otherwise regenerate against the old
          # binary and open a pull request that changes nothing
          if [[ "$(make -s datastore-version)" != "$LATEST" ]]; then
            echo "config still pins $(make -s datastore-version)" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

          # the definition this plugin ships and the readme both come from the
          # binary, so they move with the pin or the drift check fails later
          make generate

          if git diff --quiet; then
            echo "nothing changed"
            echo "changed=false" >>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "changed=true" >>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
        env:
          LATEST: ${{ steps.versions.outputs.latest }}

      - name: Open a pull request
        if: steps.bump.outputs.changed == 'true'
        run: |
          git config user.name 'Dokku Bot'
          git config user.email no-reply@dokku.com
          git checkout -b "$BRANCH"
          git add -A
          git commit --quiet --message "chore: upgrade dokku-datastore to $LATEST"
          git push --quiet origin "$BRANCH"

          gh pr create \
            --title "chore: upgrade dokku-datastore to $LATEST" \
            --body "$(printf '%s\n\n%s' \
              "Picks up https://github.com/dokku/dokku-datastore/releases/tag/$LATEST." \
              "The definition this plugin ships and the readme are generated from the binary, so they move with the pin.")"
        env:
          BRANCH: ${{ steps.versions.outputs.branch }}
          LATEST: ${{ steps.versions.outputs.latest }}

---
services:
  clickhouse:
    image: "{{ .Image }}:{{ .ImageVersion }}"

    # the image creates the database and the account from these on first boot
    environment:
      CLICKHOUSE_DB: "{{ .Database }}"
      CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"
      CLICKHOUSE_USER: "{{ .ServiceName }}"

    volumes:
      # this mounts over the directory the image keeps its own configuration
      # in, which is why the pre create hook copies that configuration out
      # first. Without it clickhouse starts with no configuration at all.
      - type: bind
        source: "{{ .HostRoot }}/config"
        target: /etc/clickhouse-server
      - type: bind
        source: "{{ .HostRoot }}/data"
        target: /var/lib/clickhouse

    ports:
      - name: native
        target: 9000
        primary: true
      - name: http
        target: 8123

x-dokku:
  plugin: clickhouse
  title: Clickhouse
  scheme: clickhouse
  alias: CLICKHOUSE

  # clickhouse answers on two ports with two protocols, and an app says which
  # it wants by overriding the scheme. The url has to follow: the http port
  # takes no database in the path, the native one does.
  dsn: >-
    {{ if eq .Scheme "http" -}}
    http://{{ .ServiceName }}:{{ .Secret.password }}@{{ .Host }}:{{ .Port.http }}
    {{- else -}}
    {{ .Scheme }}://{{ .ServiceName }}:{{ .Secret.password }}@{{ .Host }}:{{ .Port.native }}/{{ .Database }}
    {{- end }}

  wait: native

  secrets:
    password:
      file: PASSWORD
      length: 16
      env: SERVICE_PASSWORD

      # the image writes the account into users.d each time it starts, from
      # CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD, so a new password is a container made again
      rebuild: true

  hooks:
    pre_create:
      # the image's own configuration, copied out before the mount hides it.
      # It runs in the service's own image, so the files are exactly the ones
      # that image ships rather than a copy this repo would have to keep up to
      # date with every version. Copied from where the image keeps it, which a
      # service moving its config volume does not change, since the hook runs
      # in a container of its own without the service's volumes.
      volumes:
        - type: bind
          source: "{{ .HostRoot }}/config"
          target: /seed
      exec:
        - sh
        - -c
        # -n so that an operator's edits are never overwritten: the files are
        # theirs once they exist
        # users.d as well as config.d: the image's entrypoint writes the
        # account it is told to create into users.d, and fails if it is not
        # there
        - >-
          mkdir -p /seed/config.d /seed/users.d &&
          cp -n /etc/clickhouse-server/config.xml /seed/config.xml &&
          cp -n /etc/clickhouse-server/users.xml /seed/users.xml &&
          cp -n /etc/clickhouse-server/config.d/docker_related_config.xml /seed/config.d/docker_related_config.xml

  commands:
    # without a terminal, as over ssh without -t, the client reads all of stdin
    # before it runs anything, so no result is shown until stdin is closed.
    # None of its options changes that.
    connect:
      exec: ["clickhouse", "client", "--user={{ .ServiceName }}", "--password={{ .Secret.password }}"]
      env:
        LANG: C.UTF-8
        LC_ALL: C.UTF-8

    # both dump verbs are vendored scripts around clickhouse's own BACKUP and
    # RESTORE, the only dump that carries every table engine, view and
    # dictionary as the server knows them. The server reads and writes the
    # archive on its own filesystem, so the scripts run beside it with the
    # service's volumes: a sidecar reaches the file the server wrote, and works
    # against a service whose container was created before the scripts existed,
    # or by the bash plugin, without recreating it first.
    #
    # The archive stores the database under a fixed name, so an export from one
    # service imports into any other, which is what clone relies on. Only
    # archives written by this export can be imported.
    #
    # The credentials go in their own variables rather than the CLICKHOUSE_
    # ones, which the image's entrypoint and the client both read for
    # themselves.
    export:
      mode: sidecar
      exec: ["dokku-clickhouse-export"]
      env:
        BACKUP_CONFIG: "{{ .Target.config }}/config.d/dokku-backups.xml"
        CONFIG_FILE: "{{ .Target.config }}/config.xml"
        DOKKU_CLICKHOUSE_DATABASE: "{{ .Database }}"
        DOKKU_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"
        DOKKU_CLICKHOUSE_USER: "{{ .ServiceName }}"

      # every database on the server under the names they have, leaving out
      # the ones it keeps for itself. The service's account is granted every
      # database rather than its own, so it can back them all up.
      all_databases:
        mode: sidecar
        exec: ["dokku-clickhouse-export"]
        env:
          BACKUP_CONFIG: "{{ .Target.config }}/config.d/dokku-backups.xml"
          CONFIG_FILE: "{{ .Target.config }}/config.xml"
          DOKKU_CLICKHOUSE_ALL_DATABASES: "true"
          DOKKU_CLICKHOUSE_DATABASE: "{{ .Database }}"
          DOKKU_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"
          DOKKU_CLICKHOUSE_USER: "{{ .ServiceName }}"

    import:
      # restored beside the live database and swapped in only once the restore
      # succeeds, so an archive that fails to restore leaves the data alone
      mode: sidecar
      stdin: true
      exec: ["dokku-clickhouse-import"]
      env:
        BACKUP_CONFIG: "{{ .Target.config }}/config.d/dokku-backups.xml"
        CONFIG_FILE: "{{ .Target.config }}/config.xml"
        DOKKU_CLICKHOUSE_DATABASE: "{{ .Database }}"
        DOKKU_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"
        DOKKU_CLICKHOUSE_USER: "{{ .ServiceName }}"

      # each database in the archive replaces the one of the same name, all of
      # them restored beside the live ones before any is swapped in
      all_databases:
        mode: sidecar
        stdin: true
        exec: ["dokku-clickhouse-import"]
        env:
          BACKUP_CONFIG: "{{ .Target.config }}/config.d/dokku-backups.xml"
          CONFIG_FILE: "{{ .Target.config }}/config.xml"
          DOKKU_CLICKHOUSE_ALL_DATABASES: "true"
          DOKKU_CLICKHOUSE_DATABASE: "{{ .Database }}"
          DOKKU_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"
          DOKKU_CLICKHOUSE_USER: "{{ .ServiceName }}"

    # the database is dropped and made again from its own SHOW CREATE, which
    # keeps its engine and comment. The account is declared in users.d rather
    # than granted on the database, so the drop leaves it able to reach the new
    # one. A staging database an import left behind goes with it. The session
    # sits in the system database, as the import's does, so it is never inside
    # the database being dropped.
    #
    # run in the service container rather than beside it, where the password
    # can go in CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD: no entrypoint runs, and the client reads it
    # from there rather than from its argv
    reset:
      exec:
        - sh
        - -c
        - |
          set -e
          database="$1"
          query() {
            clickhouse client --user "$DOKKU_CLICKHOUSE_USER" --database system --query "$1"
          }
          create="$(query "SHOW CREATE DATABASE \`$database\` FORMAT TSVRaw")"
          query "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS \`${database}_dokku_import\` SYNC"
          query "DROP DATABASE \`$database\` SYNC"
          query "$create"
        - dokku-clickhouse-reset
        - "{{ .Database }}"
      env:
        CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD: "{{ .Secret.password }}"
        DOKKU_CLICKHOUSE_USER: "{{ .ServiceName }}"

  # the databases the server keeps for itself. default is left out: it is only
  # the default database, and a service named after it works
  reserved_names: [information_schema, system]

HARDWARE = $(shell uname -m)
SYSTEM_NAME  = $(shell uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
ARCH = $(shell dpkg --print-architecture)
SHFMT_VERSION = 3.0.2
XUNIT_TO_GITHUB_VERSION = 0.3.0
XUNIT_READER_VERSION = 0.1.0

PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX = clickhouse
DOKKU_DATASTORE_VERSION = $(shell sed -n 's/^export DOKKU_DATASTORE_VERSION=.*:-\(.*\)}"$$/\1/p' config)
ifeq ($(HARDWARE),aarch64)
	DOKKU_DATASTORE_ARCH = arm64
else ifeq ($(HARDWARE),arm64)
	DOKKU_DATASTORE_ARCH = arm64
else
	DOKKU_DATASTORE_ARCH = amd64
endif

# the readme is generated by the same binary the plugin runs, which is already
# installed on a host running dokku and is fetched into tmp everywhere else
INSTALLED_DOKKU_DATASTORE = $(wildcard /var/lib/dokku/data/$(PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX)/dokku-datastore)
ifeq ($(INSTALLED_DOKKU_DATASTORE),)
	DOKKU_DATASTORE = tmp/dokku-datastore
else
	DOKKU_DATASTORE = $(INSTALLED_DOKKU_DATASTORE)
endif


bats:
ifeq ($(SYSTEM_NAME),darwin)
ifneq ($(shell bats --version >/dev/null 2>&1 ; echo $$?),0)
	brew install bats-core
endif
else
	git clone https://github.com/bats-core/bats-core.git /tmp/bats
	cd /tmp/bats && sudo ./install.sh /usr/local
	rm -rf /tmp/bats
endif

shellcheck:
ifneq ($(shell shellcheck --version >/dev/null 2>&1 ; echo $$?),0)
ifeq ($(SYSTEM_NAME),darwin)
	brew install shellcheck
else
ifeq ($(ARCH),arm64)
  sudo add-apt-repository 'deb http://ports.ubuntu.com/ubuntu-ports jammy-backports main restricted universe multiverse'
else
  sudo add-apt-repository 'deb http://archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu jammy-backports main restricted universe multiverse'
endif
	sudo rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* && sudo apt-get clean
	sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -qq -y shellcheck
endif
endif

shfmt:
ifneq ($(shell shfmt --version >/dev/null 2>&1 ; echo $$?),0)
ifeq ($(shfmt),Darwin)
	brew install shfmt
else
	wget -qO /tmp/shfmt https://github.com/mvdan/sh/releases/download/v$(SHFMT_VERSION)/shfmt_v$(SHFMT_VERSION)_linux_amd64
	chmod +x /tmp/shfmt
	sudo mv /tmp/shfmt /usr/local/bin/shfmt
endif
endif

readlink:
ifeq ($(shell uname),Darwin)
ifeq ($(shell greadlink > /dev/null 2>&1 ; echo $$?),127)
	brew install coreutils
endif
	ln -nfs `which greadlink` tests/bin/readlink
endif

ci-dependencies: shellcheck bats readlink

lint-setup:
	@mkdir -p tmp/test-results/shellcheck tmp/shellcheck
	@find . -not -path '*/\.*' -type f | xargs file | grep text | awk -F ':' '{ print $$1 }' | xargs head -n1 | egrep -B1 "bash" | grep "==>" | awk '{ print $$2 }' > tmp/shellcheck/test-files
	@cat tests/shellcheck-exclude | sed -n -e '/^# SC/p' | cut -d' ' -f2 | paste -d, -s - > tmp/shellcheck/exclude

lint: lint-setup
	# these are disabled due to their expansive existence in the codebase. we should clean it up though
	@cat tests/shellcheck-exclude | sed -n -e '/^# SC/p'
	@echo linting...
	@cat tmp/shellcheck/test-files | xargs shellcheck -e $(shell cat tmp/shellcheck/exclude) | tests/shellcheck-to-junit --output tmp/test-results/shellcheck/results.xml --files tmp/shellcheck/test-files --exclude $(shell cat tmp/shellcheck/exclude)

unit-tests:
	@echo running unit tests...
	@mkdir -p tmp/test-results/bats
	@cd tests && echo "executing tests: $(shell cd tests ; ls *.bats | xargs)"
	cd tests && bats --report-formatter junit --timing -o ../tmp/test-results/bats *.bats

tmp/dokku-datastore:
	mkdir -p tmp
	curl -o tmp/dokku-datastore -sL --fail https://github.com/dokku/dokku-datastore/releases/download/$(DOKKU_DATASTORE_VERSION)/dokku-datastore-$(SYSTEM_NAME)-$(DOKKU_DATASTORE_ARCH)
	chmod +x tmp/dokku-datastore

tmp/xunit-reader:
	mkdir -p tmp
	curl -o tmp/xunit-reader.tgz -sL https://github.com/josegonzalez/go-xunit-reader/releases/download/v$(XUNIT_READER_VERSION)/xunit-reader_$(XUNIT_READER_VERSION)_$(SYSTEM_NAME)_$(HARDWARE).tgz
	tar xf tmp/xunit-reader.tgz -C tmp
	chmod +x tmp/xunit-reader

setup:
	bash tests/setup.sh
	$(MAKE) ci-dependencies

test: lint unit-tests

report: tmp/xunit-reader
	tmp/xunit-reader -p 'tmp/test-results/bats/*.xml'
	tmp/xunit-reader -p 'tmp/test-results/shellcheck/*.xml'

.PHONY: clean
clean:
	rm -f README.md
	rm -rf datastore

.PHONY: generate
generate: clean datastore README.md

# the definitions this plugin ships, written from the binary that runs them. They
# are generated output like the readme, so CI fails if what is committed differs.
.PHONY: datastore
datastore: $(DOKKU_DATASTORE)
	$(DOKKU_DATASTORE) generate --plugin-dir . $(PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX)

# the version pinned in config, for anything that needs to read it back. Reading
# it here rather than repeating the expression keeps one definition of where the
# pin lives.
.PHONY: datastore-version
datastore-version:
	@echo $(DOKKU_DATASTORE_VERSION)

.PHONY: README.md
README.md: $(DOKKU_DATASTORE)
	$(DOKKU_DATASTORE) readme $(PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX) > README.md

FROM dokku/dokku:latest

RUN apt-get update
RUN apt-get install --no-install-recommends -y build-essential file nano && \
  apt-get clean autoclean && \
  apt-get autoremove --yes && \
  rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* && \
  mkdir -p /mnt/dokku/home/dokku /mnt/dokku/var/lib/dokku/config /mnt/dokku/var/lib/dokku/data /mnt/dokku/var/lib/dokku/services && \
  chown -R dokku:dokku /mnt/dokku/home/dokku /mnt/dokku/var/lib/dokku/config /mnt/dokku/var/lib/dokku/data /mnt/dokku/var/lib/dokku/services && \
  echo "dokku.me" > /home/dokku/VHOST

ADD https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dokku/dokku/master/tests/dhparam.pem /mnt/dokku/etc/nginx/dhparam.pem

COPY .devcontainer/20_init_plugin /etc/my_init.d/20_init_plugin
COPY .devcontainer/bin/ /usr/local/bin/

COPY . .

RUN source /tmp/config && \
  echo "export ${PLUGIN_DISABLE_PULL_VARIABLE}=true" > /tmp/.env && \
  echo "export PLUGIN_NAME=${PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX}" >> /tmp/.env && \
  echo "export PLUGIN_VARIABLE=${PLUGIN_VARIABLE}" >> /tmp/.env

RUN source /tmp/.env && \
  dokku plugin:install file:///tmp --name $PLUGIN_NAME && \
  make ci-dependencies

#!/usr/bin/env bash
source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/config"
source "$PLUGIN_CORE_AVAILABLE_PATH/common/functions"
set -eo pipefail
[[ $DOKKU_TRACE ]] && set -x

# installed-datastore-version reports the version a binary says it is, and nothing
# at all when there is no such file or it cannot be run.
installed-datastore-version() {
  declare BINARY="$1"

  if [[ ! -x "$BINARY" ]]; then
    return 0
  fi

  # a file that is executable but is not this binary exits non-zero, and under
  # errexit the assignment that takes this would end the install saying nothing.
  # Reporting no version is the useful answer: it is what a caller checks for.
  "$BINARY" version 2>/dev/null | head -n1 | tr -d '[:space:]' || true
}

plugin-install() {
  local ARCHITECTURE="amd64"
  if [[ "$(uname -m)" == "aarch64" ]]; then
    ARCHITECTURE="arm64"
  fi

  local DOKKU_DATASTORE_ROOT="${DOKKU_LIB_ROOT}/data/${PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX}"
  local DOKKU_DATASTORE_BINARY="${DOKKU_DATASTORE_ROOT}/dokku-datastore-${DOKKU_DATASTORE_VERSION}"
  local DOKKU_DATASTORE_LOCAL="${DOKKU_DATASTORE_ROOT}/dokku-datastore.local"
  local DOKKU_DATASTORE_URL="https://github.com/dokku/dokku-datastore/releases/download/${DOKKU_DATASTORE_VERSION}/dokku-datastore-linux-${ARCHITECTURE}"

  # the binary has to be in place before anything else, because the rest of the
  # install is the binary's own trigger-install command
  mkdir -p "$DOKKU_DATASTORE_ROOT" || dokku_log_fail "Unable to create the ${PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX} plugin data directory"
  chown -R "${DOKKU_SYSTEM_USER}:${DOKKU_SYSTEM_GROUP}" "$DOKKU_DATASTORE_ROOT"

  # a binary staged here wins over the pinned release, so that an unreleased
  # build can be tested against this plugin. stage one with
  # `make setup DOKKU_DATASTORE_BINARY=/path/to/dokku-datastore`
  if [[ -x "$DOKKU_DATASTORE_LOCAL" ]]; then
    dokku_log_info1_quiet "Installing dokku-datastore from ${DOKKU_DATASTORE_LOCAL}"
    cp "$DOKKU_DATASTORE_LOCAL" "${DOKKU_DATASTORE_ROOT}/dokku-datastore"
    chmod +x "${DOKKU_DATASTORE_ROOT}/dokku-datastore"
    "${DOKKU_DATASTORE_ROOT}/dokku-datastore" trigger-install "$PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX"
    return
  fi

  # the binary is asked what it is rather than believed on the strength of its
  # filename. A truncated download, a binary for the wrong architecture, one left
  # by hand, or a release that was re-tagged all look correct to a name check and
  # would then be used for as long as the version stayed pinned
  if [[ "$(installed-datastore-version "$DOKKU_DATASTORE_BINARY")" != "$DOKKU_DATASTORE_VERSION" ]]; then
    dokku_log_info1_quiet "Installing dokku-datastore@${DOKKU_DATASTORE_VERSION}"

    # download to a temporary path so that a failed request cannot leave a file
    # behind that the check above would take for an installed binary
    if ! curl -sSL --fail "${DOKKU_DATASTORE_URL}" -o "${DOKKU_DATASTORE_BINARY}.download"; then
      rm -f "${DOKKU_DATASTORE_BINARY}.download"
      dokku_log_fail "Unable to download dokku-datastore@${DOKKU_DATASTORE_VERSION} from ${DOKKU_DATASTORE_URL}"
    fi

    # made executable before it is asked its version, because curl writes it
    # without the bit and a file that cannot run reports nothing
    chmod +x "${DOKKU_DATASTORE_BINARY}.download"

    local DOWNLOADED_VERSION
    DOWNLOADED_VERSION="$(installed-datastore-version "${DOKKU_DATASTORE_BINARY}.download")"
    if [[ "$DOWNLOADED_VERSION" != "$DOKKU_DATASTORE_VERSION" ]]; then
      rm -f "${DOKKU_DATASTORE_BINARY}.download"
      dokku_log_fail "Downloaded dokku-datastore reports '${DOWNLOADED_VERSION}' rather than ${DOKKU_DATASTORE_VERSION}"
    fi

    mv "${DOKKU_DATASTORE_BINARY}.download" "$DOKKU_DATASTORE_BINARY"
  fi

  cp "$DOKKU_DATASTORE_BINARY" "${DOKKU_DATASTORE_ROOT}/dokku-datastore"
  chmod +x "${DOKKU_DATASTORE_ROOT}/dokku-datastore"

  "${DOKKU_DATASTORE_ROOT}/dokku-datastore" trigger-install "$PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX"
}
plugin-install "$@"

service-backup-unschedule-cmd() {
  declare desc="unschedule the backup of the $PLUGIN_SERVICE service"
  local cmd="$PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX:backup-unschedule" argv=("$@")
  [[ ${argv[0]} == "$cmd" ]] && shift 1

  "${DOKKU_LIB_ROOT}/data/${PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX}/dokku-datastore" backup-unschedule "$PLUGIN_COMMAND_PREFIX" "$@"
}

service-backup-unschedule-cmd "$@"
